indicators.markdownDescription:
List of strings that, when matched at the start of a log line's text, designate it as a group head.

A list of strings that, when matched at the start of a log line's text, designate it as a group head. Unmatched lines default to `false`, indicating they are group children.  - `192.` - Indicates a private IP address, common in web server logs (e.g., "192.168.1.1 - - [...]"). - `10.` - Indicates a private IP range, often in Kubernetes or internal network logs (e.g., "10.244.0.125 - - [...]"). - `GET ` - Indicates an HTTP GET request, marking the start of a web transaction log (e.g., "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1"). - `\x1b[2m` - Indicates a line that opens in ANSI dim, the way Rust tracing prints the timestamp of a coloured line. The escape code is glued to the year, so the timestamp is not recognised and the line needs this indicator to head its own event. - `at ` - Indicates a Java/C# stack trace continuation.

childLabels.markdownDescription:
Labels that mark a line as a child of the event above it, even when the line has its own timestamp.

A list of labels that mark a line as a child of the event above it in the same stream, even when the line has its own timestamp. Empty by default.  A line's label is the word before its first colon followed by two spaces, where that word starts the line or follows a space, a colon or a closing bracket. PostgreSQL writes its log prefix and then a label such as `ERROR:  ` or `DETAIL:  ` on each line of one error, so the `ERROR` line heads the event and the lines below it join that event. The shipped configuration lists:  - `DETAIL`, `HINT`, `CONTEXT` and `STATEMENT`: PostgreSQL lines that add to the error or message above them. - `QUERY` and `LOCATION`: PostgreSQL lines that give the internal query and the source location of the error above them.  The rule reads the line's own text, once per template, so a line's place in its event holds across restarts and nodes.

negators.markdownDescription:
List of patterns that mark a line as a known continuation (e.g., stack trace lines), negating standalone status.

A list of strings that, when matched at the start of a log line's text, mark it as a known continuation line. Lines matching these patterns are identified as continuations (e.g., stack trace frames) and will not have message patterns calculated for them, optimizing processing performance.  - `	at ` - Java/Kotlin stack trace frame (tab-prefixed). - `   at ` - .NET stack trace frame (space-prefixed). - `  File "` - Python stack trace frame. - `    at ` - Node.js stack trace frame. - `Caused by:` - Java chained exception. - `	... ` - Java truncated stack frames.
